answer:
Start with  
\[
\left[\frac11,\frac21\right].
\]
To compare \(\sqrt2\) with a positive reduced fraction \(p/q\), use only integers:
\[
\sqrt2<\frac pq \iff 2q^2<p^2,\qquad
\sqrt2>\frac pq \iff 2q^2>p^2.
\]
Equality cannot occur because \(\sqrt2\) is irrational.

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{Step} & \text{current interval} & \text{mediant }p/q & \text{integer test} & \text{keep}\\ \hline
1 & \left[\frac11,\frac21\right] & \frac32 & 2\cdot2^2=8<9=3^2 & \left[\frac11,\frac32\right]\\[2mm]
2 & \left[\frac11,\frac32\right] & \frac43 & 2\cdot3^2=18>16=4^2 & \left[\frac43,\frac32\right]\\[2mm]
3 & \left[\frac43,\frac32\right] & \frac75 & 2\cdot5^2=50>49=7^2 & \left[\frac75,\frac32\right]\\[2mm]
4 & \left[\frac75,\frac32\right] & \frac{10}{7} & 2\cdot7^2=98<100=10^2 & \left[\frac75,\frac{10}{7}\right]\\[2mm]
5 & \left[\frac75,\frac{10}{7}\right] & \frac{17}{12} & 2\cdot12^2=288<289=17^2 & \left[\frac75,\frac{17}{12}\right]\\[2mm]
6 & \left[\frac75,\frac{17}{12}\right] & \frac{24}{17} & 2\cdot17^2=578>576=24^2 & \left[\frac{24}{17},\frac{17}{12}\right]
\end{array}
\]

Thus the final bracket is
\[
\boxed{\left[\frac{24}{17},\frac{17}{12}\right]}.
\]
Indeed,
\[
\left(\frac{24}{17}\right)^2=\frac{576}{289}<2
<\frac{289}{144}=\left(\frac{17}{12}\right)^2,
\]
so it contains \(\sqrt2\). All listed endpoints are reduced fractions, and every decision was made by comparing integers such as \(p^2\) and \(2q^2\); no decimal approximation or rounding of \(\sqrt2\) was needed.
